profile.address: Oakland County, MI (approximately 18 miles from downtown Detroit)
profile.reading: EdgeConneX Detroit, internally coded DET01 per the operator own market page, sits in Oakland County, Michigan, roughly 18 miles from downtown Detroit. The facility totals 39,900 square feet with 9,930 square feet of raised floor space for tenant racks, built to a Tier 3 design with N plus 1 redundancy. No overall megawatt capacity figure, opening year, or named tenant is disclosed on EdgeConneX own site. Several network-partnership announcements have been made for this location, including the Detroit Internet Exchange offering direct-route connectivity into the facility, Console Connect deploying its enterprise interconnection platform there, and an earlier partnership bringing Packet bare-metal edge cloud and Sprint Curiosity IoT platform capabilities to the site, none of which name an underlying anchor tenant. EdgeConneX is a US-based edge and build-to-suit data center operator founded in 2009 and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia, with regional headquarters in Amsterdam and Singapore. The company was acquired by EQT Infrastructure in 2020, and its board also includes a representative of Sixth Street, an investment firm, alongside EQT partners, though exact ownership percentages are not disclosed publicly. EdgeConneX describes its footprint today as more than 90 data centers across more than 60 markets in over 20 countries on four continents, and it operates a joint venture called AdaniConneX in India alongside a strategic investment in the China-based operator Chayora. EdgeConneX naming convention across its US markets typically pairs an airport-code-style market abbreviation, such as DET for Detroit, CHI for Chicago, POR for Portland, and SDG for San Diego, with a sequential building number, a shorthand common across the colocation and edge-computing industry for quickly identifying a facility market and build order. Oakland County broader economic profile as a suburban Detroit business and technology corridor is consistent with EdgeConneX stated rationale of siting the facility roughly 18 miles outside the city core while still serving the wider metro area.
profile.research_note: 39,900 sqft total / 9,930 sqft raised floor, Tier 3 N+1 design, and DET01 designation confirmed via EdgeConneX own Detroit market page. No MW, year-opened, or tenant disclosed.

reading.body:
EdgeConneX DET01 in Michigan publishes 39,900 square feet of technical space but no IT power capacity in megawatts, making AI hosting potential impossible to assess from available data.

The facility holds five compliance certifications: ENERGY STAR, HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI-DSS, and ISO 27001. These credentials qualify it for regulated workloads in healthcare, payments, and enterprise security. They do not indicate suitability for high-density GPU clusters. Which tenants occupy the space and what workloads run there remain unpublished, so the compliance posture cannot predict whether this is a venue for frontier AI training or for traditional enterprise computing.

Michigan has six data center facilities on record. None of the six publishes a megawatt figure. DET01's published capacity is therefore zero by the metric that determines AI infrastructure utility: power. Without a power specification from the operator, the facility cannot be ranked or compared on the scale that governs AI compute density, cooling requirements, and grid impact. Square footage alone does not constrain AI scaling. Power does.
